name: a_econ_data
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: Economic data.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Every US economic release on the session date and the brief date through the cutoff (PMIs, jobless claims, durable goods, housing, GDP, inflation, sentiment): actual vs consensus vs prior, and release time.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **Macro / Calendar**

- **Nonfarm payrolls** increased by **29,000** in September versus **90,000 consensus** and **162,000 prior**; the prior two months were revised down by a combined **60,000**. The release was at **08:30 ET on October 2** (BLS, Oct. 2 08:30 ET; Brown Brothers Harriman, Oct. 4 12:20 ET).[5][3]
- The **unemployment rate** rose to **4.2%** in September versus **4.1% consensus** and **4.1% prior**; the **labor-force participation rate** was **61.8%** versus **61.4% consensus** and **61.6% prior**. The release was at **08:30 ET on October 2** (BLS, Oct. 2 08:30 ET).[6][10]
- **Private payrolls** increased by **20,000** in September versus **85,000 consensus** and **127,000 prior**; **government payrolls** increased by **9,000** versus **15,000 consensus** and **35,000 prior** (BLS, Oct. 2 08:30 ET).[5]
- **Manufacturing payrolls** increased by **9,000** in September versus **10,000 consensus** and **16,000 prior**; average weekly hours were **34.3** versus **34.3 consensus** and **34.4 prior** (BLS, Oct. 2 08:30 ET).[5][10]
- **Average hourly earnings** increased **0.3% month over month** versus **0.3% consensus** and **0.3% prior**, and increased **3.2% year over year** versus **3.2% consensus** and **3.1% prior** (BLS, Oct. 2 08:30 ET).[5]
- **Factory orders** increased **0.1% month over month** in August versus **0.1% consensus** and **0.8% prior, revised from 0.9%**; **factory orders excluding transportation** increased **0.3%** versus **0.3% consensus** and **0.7% prior**. The release was at **10:00 ET on October 2** (U.S. Census Bureau, Oct. 2 10:00 ET; RTT News, Oct. 2 10:16 ET).[9][10]
- **Durable-goods orders** were **0.0% month over month** in August versus **0.0% prior**; durable goods excluding transportation increased **0.3%**, and nondefense capital-goods orders excluding aircraft increased **1.6%** (U.S. Census Bureau, Oct. 2 10:00 ET).[10]
- **S&P Global final services PMI** for September was scheduled for **09:45 ET on October 5**, with **58.7 consensus** and **58.7 prior**; the available calendar result did not report an actual by the **12:20 ET cutoff** (S&P Global, Oct. 5 09:45 ET).[1]
- **S&P Global final composite PMI** for September was scheduled for **09:45 ET on October 5**, with **58.4 consensus** and **56.0 prior**; the available calendar result did not report an actual by the **12:20 ET cutoff** (S&P Global, Oct. 5 09:45 ET).[7]
- **ISM services PMI** for September was scheduled for **10:00 ET on October 5**, with **55.1 consensus** and **55.4 prior**; the available calendar result did not report an actual by the **12:20 ET cutoff** (Institute for Supply Management, Oct. 5 10:00 ET).[1][4]
- The September **ISM services subindexes** had prior readings of **61.7 for business activity**, **60.9 for new orders**, **47.8 for employment**, and **72.6 for prices**; no actual September readings were available by **12:20 ET on October 5** (Institute for Supply Management, Oct. 5 10:00 ET).[7][8]
- The **Employment Trends Index** for September was scheduled for **10:00 ET on October 5**, with **108.53 prior**; no actual was available by the **12:20 ET cutoff** (The Conference Board, Oct. 5 10:00 ET).[15]
